content:
Hello, I’m Gerald Höhn, a mathematician at Kansas State University working primarily on vertex operator algebras and related finite groups.

I would like to share my project A constructive ATLAS of finite simple groups in Lean.

Research note / current public manuscript:
https://zenodo.org/records/22986720

Source repository:
https://github.com/Moonshine-in-Kansas/atlas

The project constructs finite simple groups from codes, lattices, forms, algebras, and finite geometries, with proofs of their orders, simplicity, and structural properties. The release described in the note covers eight families and fifteen sporadic groups. The aim is the construction side of finite simple group theory, not the exhaustiveness proof of the classification.

The work combines classical constructions with new mathematical arguments. Lean serves as a verification tool rather than being the subject of the research. Both the Lean implementation and the manuscript text were generated by AI under my mathematical direction; I take responsibility for the mathematical specifications and claims. The repository contains the catalogue and verification material.

For the Monster and Baby Monster, I plan to formalize the necessary theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs) and use it to formalize their constructions and group-theoretic properties. This is future work, not part of the completed release.

I would welcome feedback, particularly on the formal theorem statements and dependency structure, and suggestions about connections with mathlib. I would also be interested to hear from anyone working on VOA formalization.

Gerald Höhn
cc @Scott Carnahan and @Kalle Kytölä for VOAs

A short follow-up: I have now submitted two companion mathematical papers providing the basis for the formalizations of the Fischer groups and the Rudvalis and Tits groups:

Fischer groups:
https://zenodo.org/records/22991689

Conway–Wales lattice, Rudvalis and Tits groups:
https://zenodo.org/records/22991122

The Rudvalis and Tits groups have now also been formalized in Lean, including proofs of their orders and simplicity. These are additions to the ongoing ATLAS development; neither was included in the frozen v1 release announced above.

The ongoing development now also covers all families of finite simple groups of types A, B, C, D and G₂, including the corresponding twisted families.

My approach emphasizes explicit constructions with proofs of order and simplicity, while retaining geometric and subgroup structure useful for further group theory. I hope these developments will be useful alongside the other CFSG formalization projects, and I would be happy to compare notes and explore what can be shared.

Hello, Gerald.
I've been formalizing fundamentals of vertex algebra theory for a few years, and while a definition following Borcherds's original paper can be implemented easily in mathlib now, we are still missing some parts that are key to making constructions.

I'll be happy to talk about design questions, but I am not interested in reading LLM output.

FYI the Challenge/Solution files from comparator do not seem to be correctly set-up: Challenge and Solution are the same file, and every theorem in that file is a reflexivity proof of a name against itself. Setting-up Comparator contract/constraints correctly (and keeping the repository free from noise/unneccessary docs, synthesizing them in the formalization.yaml file) will enable people to give you more feedback. see https://github.com/leanprover/comparator

Thanks, Matteo. I think the current setup under verification/existence/ now addresses the Comparator issue you pointed out: Challenge.lean and Solution.lean are separate, with the challenge containing only the theorem statement and the solution providing the ATLAS construction and proof. The current status, with links to the individual Challenge/Solution files, is here:

https://github.com/Moonshine-in-Kansas/atlas/blob/main/verification/existence/RESULTS.md
